methodologyNote: Planning bands for Florida residential work. Synthesized from public industry cost guides, Florida market premiums (wind code, insurance-driven remodels, coastal access), and conservative homeowner ranges. Not contractor bids. Update this file only — matching code stays unchanged.
disclaimer: Conceptual planning ranges only — not a formal bid, quote, or guarantee. Actual costs depend on site conditions, materials, labor markets, permits, and scope. Always get written bids from licensed contractors.

ranges.unitNote: Compact kitchen refresh · ~80–140 sq ft work zone

bandHints.low: Reface or stock cabinets, keep layout, laminate or entry quartz, reuse appliances where possible
bandHints.mid: New stock/semi-custom cabinets, mid quartz, standard appliance package, minor lighting
bandHints.high: Better cabinets and surfaces, new appliances mid-tier, limited electrical updates

ranges.unitNote: Full remodel of a standard kitchen · ~150–250 sq ft

bandHints.low: Full gut with stock cabinets, keep major plumbing runs, mid-grade finishes
bandHints.mid: Semi-custom cabinets, quartz, layout tweak (island or peninsulas), mid appliances
bandHints.high: Higher millwork, better appliances, more electrical/lighting, modest structural opening

drivers: Full cabinetry replacement and finish level
Florida electrical/code upgrades in older homes

ranges.unitNote: Large or premium custom kitchen · openings, island, high finishes

bandHints.low: Large footprint with semi-custom work, one structural opening, good not luxury appliances
bandHints.mid: Custom/semi-custom millwork, premium quartz or stone, strong appliance package
bandHints.high: Full custom millwork, luxury appliances, multiple openings, high-end lighting and stone

drivers: High-end surfaces, lighting, and smart controls

ranges.unitNote: Guest / hall bath refresh · limited layout change

bandHints.low: Vanity/fixture swap, paint, simple shower curtain or keep tub surround
bandHints.mid: New vanity, toilet, tile floor or tub surround, standard glass or curtain
bandHints.high: Better tile package, framed glass, upgraded fixtures, modest lighting

drivers: Keep tub vs convert to walk-in shower

ranges.unitNote: Full gut of one bathroom · standard primary or large hall bath

bandHints.low: Full gut, keep layout, mid tile and fixtures, acrylic or basic tile shower
bandHints.mid: New shower system, solid waterproofing, mid tile walls/floor, dual vanity optional
bandHints.high: Custom tile patterns, better glass, heated floor or niche package, nicer fixtures

drivers: Tile coverage (floor only vs full wet walls)

ranges.unitNote: Luxury primary suite bath · layout change possible

bandHints.low: Layout change with solid mid-high finishes, freestanding or large shower
bandHints.mid: Dual vanity, custom tile, quality glass, better fixtures and lighting
bandHints.high: Spa-level finishes, heated floors, steam options, complex tile and stone

drivers: Moving walls, drains, or enlarging wet areas
Luxury fixtures, heated floors, ventilation upgrades

ranges.unitNote: Selective multi-room renovation · not whole-house gut

bandHints.low: A few key rooms with cosmetic + light systems work
bandHints.mid: Kitchen or baths plus flooring/paint throughout living areas
bandHints.high: Multiple wet areas or partial systems upgrades with better finishes

drivers: How many rooms and wet areas are in scope
Cosmetic finishes vs systems (electric, HVAC, plumbing)
Age and condition of the home
Whether permits and Florida code upgrades are triggered

ranges.unitNote: Whole-home remodel · moderate scope on a typical single-family house

bandHints.low: Kitchen + baths + floors/paint; keep most walls and systems where legal
bandHints.mid: Full interior refresh, kitchen/baths, targeted HVAC/electrical, mid finishes
bandHints.high: More reconfiguration, higher finishes, broader systems work

drivers: Kitchen and bath count and finish level
HVAC, electrical panel, and impact/energy upgrades
Florida wind and energy code when openings change

ranges.unitNote: Extensive renovation or near-rebuild interior scope

bandHints.low: Major reconfiguration with solid mid-high finishes
bandHints.mid: Structural moves, premium kitchens/baths, systems overhaul
bandHints.high: Near full rebuild quality finishes and complex architecture

ranges.unitNote: Simple room addition · roughly 200–400 sq ft

bandHints.low: Simple rectangular add, basic foundation, mid interior finishes
bandHints.mid: Better tie-in to roof/exterior, finished bedroom or office quality
bandHints.high: Higher exterior match, better windows, nicer interior package

drivers: Interior finish level and HVAC extension

ranges.unitNote: Multi-room addition · roughly 400–800 sq ft

bandHints.low: Straightforward multi-room footprint, mid finishes
bandHints.mid: Full bath or kitchenette possible, matched exterior, proper HVAC
bandHints.high: Complex rooflines, higher exterior package, better interiors

ranges.unitNote: Major wing or second-story expansion

bandHints.low: Large single-story wing with solid mid finishes
bandHints.mid: Second story or large wing with engineering and mid-high finishes
bandHints.high: Complex second story, premium exterior/interior, difficult site

drivers: Premium exterior materials and impact glazing

ranges.unitNote: Partial lower-level / walkout finish (uncommon in much of Florida)

bandHints.low: One zone: framing, drywall, basic electric and floor
bandHints.mid: Larger zone with better finishes and lighting
bandHints.high: Partial wet area or higher finish package

drivers: Moisture and humidity control (critical in FL climates)
Whether a bath or wet bar is included

ranges.unitNote: Full lower-level living area with basic wet space

bandHints.low: Full finish with basic bath rough-in or half bath
bandHints.mid: Full bath, better floors/ceilings, proper HVAC zoning
bandHints.high: Higher finishes, media wiring, nicer wet area

ranges.unitNote: Premium entertainment / suite-quality lower level

bandHints.low: Theater or suite quality on a moderate footprint
bandHints.mid: Multiple rooms, full bath, strong AV/electrical
bandHints.high: Spa-like wet areas, premium acoustics, complex systems

drivers: Sound isolation, lighting, and smart systems

ranges.unitNote: Small home, simple geometry, or partial reroof

bandHints.low: Simple gable, architectural shingles, limited tear-off
bandHints.mid: Full small home, one layer tear-off, standard underlayment
bandHints.high: Steeper pitch, more tear-off, better shingle or starter metal

drivers: Number of layers to tear off
Florida secondary water barrier / underlayment choices

ranges.unitNote: Typical single-family reroof · common Florida suburban home

bandHints.low: Straightforward shingle reroof, good access, standard underlayment
bandHints.mid: Full tear-off, redeck as needed, wind-mitigation detail, mid shingles
bandHints.high: More complex shape, partial metal accents, higher underlayment package

drivers: Shingle vs entry metal vs entry tile decisions

ranges.unitNote: Large, multi-story, tile, or premium metal system

bandHints.low: Larger shingle or simple metal on bigger footprint
bandHints.mid: Tile or quality metal, complex valleys, strong underlayment
bandHints.high: Premium tile/metal, multi-story, difficult access, extensive deck work

drivers: Secondary water barrier and Florida product approvals

ranges.unitNote: Partial elevation, repair, or limited re-clad

bandHints.low: Repair + paint or small elevation re-clad
bandHints.mid: One full elevation re-clad with proper moisture barrier
bandHints.high: Larger partial re-clad with better materials and trim

drivers: Material choice (fiber cement, stucco repair, engineered)

ranges.unitNote: Full exterior cladding update on a typical home

bandHints.low: Full re-side or stucco refresh with mid materials
bandHints.mid: Full system with moisture barrier, flashings, trim package
bandHints.high: Higher materials, more openings/trim, harder access

drivers: Full moisture barrier and flashing quality
Stucco system vs siding product tier

ranges.unitNote: Premium whole-house exterior · multi-story or mixed materials

bandHints.low: Premium materials on a full house with good access
bandHints.mid: Mixed materials, multi-story, strong detailing
bandHints.high: Stone/engineered systems, difficult access, combined window package

ranges.unitNote: Small deck, patio cover, or simple outdoor platform

bandHints.low: Simple wood deck or cover, basic railing
bandHints.mid: Composite boards or nicer railing, modest size
bandHints.high: Better structure, lighting prep, higher materials

drivers: Permit and fastener requirements in coastal zones

ranges.unitNote: Covered outdoor living area · mid size

bandHints.low: Larger deck or simple covered patio
bandHints.mid: Covered structure, fans/lighting electrical, mid finishes
bandHints.high: Screen package options, better roof, nicer flooring

drivers: Electrical for fans, outlets, and lighting

ranges.unitNote: Full outdoor pavilion · kitchen, roof, and screening possible

bandHints.low: Substantial covered living without full outdoor kitchen
bandHints.mid: Kitchen package, solid roof, screening, good finishes
bandHints.high: Full pavilion with premium cooking, structure, and finishes

drivers: Structural roof and Florida wind design
Screen rooms or aluminum specialty structures

ranges.unitNote: Compact custom home or modest knockdown · rough order of magnitude

bandHints.low: Efficient plan, mid finishes, simpler site
bandHints.mid: Solid custom finishes, impact windows, standard site work
bandHints.high: Better finishes and tougher site or design

drivers: Florida wind / energy / impact product requirements
Finish level and soft costs (design, permits)

ranges.unitNote: Mid-size custom or knockdown · roughly 3,000–4,500 sq ft class

bandHints.low: Efficient custom with mid-high finishes
bandHints.mid: Typical custom package, impact glazing, good site work
bandHints.high: Higher architecture and finish, tougher lots

drivers: Gross living area and roof complexity

ranges.unitNote: Large custom / estate-scale rebuild · wide variance

bandHints.low: Large home with controlled design and finishes
bandHints.mid: Estate-level architecture and systems
bandHints.high: Complex architecture, premium everything, difficult site

drivers: Site work, pools, and exterior packages (often separate)
Luxury finishes and long construction schedules

ranges.unitNote: Small multi-trade or GC-coordinated job · highly variable

bandHints.low: Limited labor-heavy scope, few material upgrades
bandHints.mid: Multi-trade small project with mid materials
bandHints.high: Broader small project with permits and better finishes

drivers: How many trades must be coordinated

ranges.unitNote: Mid-size general contracting project

bandHints.low: Defined multi-trade scope with mid materials
bandHints.mid: Typical GC coordination across several rooms/systems
bandHints.high: Broader mid project with higher finishes or unknowns

ranges.unitNote: Large or multi-phase GC project · planning band only

bandHints.low: Large but well-defined multi-phase work
bandHints.mid: Complex multi-phase with mid-high finishes
bandHints.high: Open-ended scope, premium finishes, heavy unknowns

drivers: Complexity and duration of multi-phase work
